::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

This page **tests very wide and tall figures in galleries and layouts**:
collages (25 × 2 inches) and tall strips grouped into galleries, as
subfigures and in a layout div. The same shapes on their own, and the
`fit` option, are on [H: wide and tall figures](h-wide.html).

Wide figures open at screen height from the left end, tall ones at
screen width from the top. Headings carry `expect-fit`, the way each image
should open. On the galleries, the browser test also checks that
Left/Right pan (or, on a tall strip, do nothing) rather than switch, and
that the previous and next buttons switch.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(200)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}

# A tall strip: `n` rows stacked, like a tall patchwork figure.
strip <- function(seed = 2, n = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  par(mfrow = c(n, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
  }
}
```

## 1. Gallery of two collages {#c1 expect-fit="height"}

Left/Right and drags pan along the collage; the previous and next
buttons switch collages.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First collage."
#|   - "Second collage."

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## 2. Gallery of two tall strips {#c2 expect-fit="width"}

Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards: Left/Right do
nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) rather than switch strips;
the previous and next buttons switch.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."

for (k in 1:2) {
  set.seed(10 + k)
  par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Strip", k, "row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
}
```

## 3. Two collages stacked (layout-nrow: 2) {#c3 expect-fit="height"}

Subfigures in a layout: each opens on its own at screen height, and the
two form a gallery.

```{r}
#| label: fig-collage-rows
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "Two collages, stacked."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage"]
#| layout-nrow: 2

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## 4. Two tall strips side by side (layout-ncol: 2) {#c4 expect-fit="width"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-strip-cols
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "Two tall strips, side by side."
#| fig-subcap: ["First strip", "Second strip"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

strip(seed = 2, n = 8)
strip(seed = 3, n = 8)
```

## 5. Tall strips in a layout div {#c5 expect-fit="width"}

A `.panzoom` div with a layout, around two separate code cells: each
strip opens on its own (no gallery: they are not subfigures).

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(seed = 4, n = 8)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(seed = 5, n = 8)
```

:::
